cards.text: Darius the Mede now rules the kingdom (Daniel 5:31), and it pleases him to appoint 120 satraps to run it, with three administrators over them. One of those three is Daniel, a man from Judah living in exile (Daniel 5:13). And friend, I can't even keep track of 120 sprinkles.

cards.question: The 120 satraps have to answer to Daniel and the other two administrators. Why does Darius set it up that way?

answers.text: So the king won't suffer loss
So the king can travel freely
So the people can bring complaints

cards.text: Then Daniel's extraordinary spirit makes him stand out among the administrators and satraps. He's that coworker who makes everybody else look like they're still hitting snooze.

cards.question: Daniel stands out so much that King Darius plans to set him over the whole ___.

cards.text: So the administrators and satraps go looking for a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom. Every record, every report, somebody's going over it with a MAGNIFYING GLASS.

cards.question: After all that digging, the administrators and satraps find some corruption in Daniel's work.
The officials come up empty on Daniel, because he is ___.

cards.text: Finally these men say it out loud: they will never find any charge against this Daniel, unless… Friend, that one little word UNLESS is carrying their WHOLE plan.

cards.question: The men say they'll never find a charge against Daniel unless they find something about what?

cards.text: So they all go to King Darius together: "O King Darius, may you live forever!" Then they tell him all the royal officials have agreed the king should make a new decree.

cards.question: For thirty days, the decree says, nobody can petition any god or man except one. Who?

cards.text: Break the decree, and you're thrown into the den of lions. And they want the king to sign it under the law of the Medes and Persians.

cards.question: Under the law of the Medes and Persians, once King Darius signs this decree, it cannot be repealed.

cards.text: King Darius signs it, and under that law, there are NO take-backs. Then Daniel learns that the document has been signed.

cards.question: Daniel knows the decree is signed. What does he do?

answers.text: He prays just as he had done before
He stops praying for thirty days
He prays only in secret at night

cards.question: Three times a day, Daniel kneels in his upper room, where the windows open toward ___.

cards.text: Then these men go as a GROUP and find Daniel petitioning and imploring his God. It took the whole crew to catch one man doing what he always does.
So the men go to King Darius and ask about his decree, like they don't already know. The king answers that by the law of the Medes and Persians, the order stands.
Then the men drop the name: Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah. They tell the king Daniel shows no regard for him or his decree, and he still makes his petition three times a day.

cards.question: As soon as King Darius hears the men say Daniel shows no regard for his decree, he is deeply ___.
King Darius works until sundown trying to rescue Daniel.

cards.text: Then the men come back together with a reminder: no decree the king establishes can be undone. So the king gives the order, and Daniel is thrown into the den of lions.

cards.question: As Daniel goes into the den, King Darius speaks to him. What does the king say?

answers.text: I am sorry it came to this
I will find a way to free you

cards.text: A stone is brought and set over the mouth of the den. Then the king seals it with his own signet ring and the rings of his nobles.

cards.question: The king seals the stone over the den so that nothing concerning Daniel could be ___.

cards.text: The king goes back to his palace and spends the night fasting, and sleep flees from him. Friend, I spent years lying awake in the back of a junk drawer, so I KNOW that kind of night.
At the first light of dawn, the king gets up and HURRIES to the den of lions. Friend, kings have people to hurry FOR them, and this one is hurrying himself.

cards.question: King Darius reaches the den and cries out to Daniel in a voice of anguish. What does he ask?

answers.text: If Daniel's God was able to deliver him
If Daniel is ready to bow to the king
If Daniel can forgive him for the decree

cards.text: And from down in the den, Daniel answers: "O king, may you live forever!" The man just spent the night with lions, and he STILL opens with his manners.

cards.question: Daniel tells the king that his God sent His ___ and shut the mouths of the lions.
Daniel says the lions have not hurt him. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He was found innocent in God's sight
He had fasted and prayed all night
He had made an offering to God

cards.text: Up top, the king is OVERJOYED and gives orders to lift Daniel out of the den. And friend, not one wound is found on him.

cards.question: No wounds at all are found on Daniel when he's lifted out of the den. What reason does the text give?

answers.text: He had trusted in his God
The king's seal had kept him safe
He had stayed awake all night

cards.text: At the king's command, the men who falsely accused Daniel are thrown into the den of lions, along with their children and wives. Before they reach the bottom of the den, the lions overpower them and crush all their bones.

Then King Darius writes to the people of every nation and language throughout the land. He decrees that in every part of his kingdom, men are to tremble in fear before the God of Daniel, and friend, THAT'S a decree worth signing.

cards.question: In his decree, Darius says the kingdom of Daniel's God will one day come to an end.
Darius's letter says Daniel's God performs signs and wonders. Where does the letter say He performs them?

answers.text: In the heavens and on the earth
In the temple and the palace

cards.text: So Daniel prospers during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus, king of Persia. The man went down into a den of lions, and he comes out of this story PROSPERING.
